checks_performed: Read only the specified source-input JSON and draft JSON; used no web or other source material.
Compared the exact unrestricted target against the draft's final writeup and audited all reductions, quantifiers, inheritance arguments, and component decompositions.

Ran check_trianglefree_wke_upto8.py using only exact integer masks and Boolean decisions. It uniquely generated every labelled triangle-free graph through order eight, reached 4,682,270 graphs at order eight, and literally verified a WKE witness for every graph.

Ran check_nine_vertex_wke_obstruction.py using only exact integer and Boolean decisions. It verified the explicit graph has 16 edges and no triangles, enumerated all 275 matchings and 33,701 eligible (M,Q) pairs, found no WKE witness, and checked all 126 five-vertex subsets.
Traced claim 10's four component classes separately and inspected the proof boundary stated in the authorized source.

claims.claim: A WKE link gives a self-contained one-vertex reduction.
claims.evidence: For a WKE witness (M,Q) in G[N(v)], take S={vxy:xy∈M} and X=M∪{vq:q∈Q}. Because M is a matching, S is edge-disjoint, and |X|=|M|+|Q|≤2|S|. Every triangle vxy is hit by xy when xy∈M and otherwise by a spoke to Q. Moreover, every S-edge outside v belongs to M⊆X. For G'=(G−X)−v, S combines with any packing of G', while X combines with any transversal of G'. Hence τ(G')≤2ν(G') implies τ(G)≤2ν(G).
claims.search_method: Direct verification from the WKE and packing/cover definitions.

claims.claim: Every graph whose every nonempty subgraph has a vertex with WKE link satisfies τ≤2ν.
claims.evidence: Induct on the vertex count. Apply claim 0 at a guaranteed vertex v. Its residual G' is a proper subgraph, and every subgraph of G' is also a subgraph of G, so the hypothesis is inherited. Induction proves the inequality for G', and the reduction transfers it to G.

claims.claim: Every locally bipartite graph satisfies τ≤2ν.
claims.evidence: For every subgraph J and v∈V(J), J[N_J(v)] is a subgraph of the bipartite graph G[N_G(v)], hence is bipartite. By König's theorem it has a matching M and a vertex cover Q with |Q|=|M|; this is a WKE witness. Thus claim 1 applies.
claims.search_method: Direct hereditary-property proof using König's matching-cover theorem.

claims.claim: Every triangle-free graph on at most eight vertices is WKE.
claims.evidence: The checker generates labelled triangle-free graphs uniquely by adjoining each new vertex with every independent earlier-neighbour set. Its guarded counts were 1, 1, 2, 7, 41, 388, 5,789, 133,501, and 4,682,270 for orders zero through eight. For every graph it exhausts every possible Q with |Q|≤⌊n/2⌋, exhausts matching extensions of the edges induced outside Q, constructs M, and literally checks M⊆E, that M is a matching, |Q|≤|M|, and that Q covers every edge outside M. Every case passed.
claims.search_method: Complete labelled-graph generation and exhaustive WKE-witness search using exact integer masks.

claims.claim: The order-eight WKE bound is sharp: a triangle-free non-WKE graph exists on nine vertices.
claims.evidence: The checker verified all 84 vertex triples and found no triangle. It generated every matching exactly once (275 total), tested every Q with |Q|≤|M| for each matching (33,701 eligible pairs), and found no WKE witness. Independently, all 126 five-vertex subsets were tested and none induced maximum degree at most one; the largest induced matching-subgraph order was four.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive literal WKE-definition search plus an independent induced-subgraph cross-check.

claims.claim: Deleting every edge that lies in no triangle preserves both ν and τ.
claims.evidence: Every original triangle retains all three edges, while deletion cannot create a triangle, so the triangle families before and after deletion are identical. Consequently their edge-disjoint packing numbers coincide, and every transversal can be restricted to triangle-edges without losing coverage, so their minimum transversal numbers also coincide.
claims.search_method: Direct comparison of the two triangle families and their optimization problems.

claims.claim: Triangle packing and covering are additive over triangle edge-overlap components.
claims.evidence: Supports of distinct triangle equivalence classes are edge-disjoint; a shared edge would itself join the classes. Therefore packings from separate supports combine without conflict, while every global transversal restricts to a transversal of each support. Conversely, unions of optimal component transversals cover every triangle. This gives ν=Σν_i and τ=Στ_i after irrelevant non-triangle edges are discarded.

claims.claim: If the triangle-edge subgraph G△ is K4-free and 8-degenerate, then τ(G)≤2ν(G).
claims.evidence: Every nonempty subgraph J⊆G△ has a vertex v of degree at most eight. Since J is K4-free, a triangle in J[N_J(v)] together with v would form a K4, so that link is triangle-free and has at most eight vertices. Claim 3 makes it WKE. Claim 1 gives τ(G△)≤2ν(G△), and claim 5 transfers the inequality to G.
claims.search_method: Direct degeneracy, link-structure, and dependency audit.

claims.claim: If G△ is K4-free and mad(G△)<9, then τ(G)≤2ν(G).
claims.evidence: Every nonempty subgraph has average degree strictly below nine, so it cannot have every degree at least nine and therefore has an integer degree at most eight. Thus G△ is 8-degenerate, and claim 7 applies.
claims.search_method: Direct average-degree-to-degeneracy proof and dependency audit.

claims.claim: A subgraph-minimal K4-free counterexample would have every edge in a triangle and minimum degree at least nine.
claims.evidence: An edge in no triangle could be deleted without changing ν or τ by claim 5, producing a smaller counterexample. If d(v)≤8, K4-freeness makes G[N(v)] triangle-free, claim 3 makes it WKE, and claim 0 reduces the assertion to a proper subgraph that satisfies the inequality by minimality. Both possibilities contradict subgraph-minimality, so every edge is triangular and δ(G)≥9.

claims.claim: The inequality holds componentwise whenever every triangle edge-overlap component has either Δ≤7, mad<7, a locally bipartite structure, or a K4-free 8-degenerate structure.
claims.evidence: Claim 6 makes the componentwise assembly valid, and claims 2 and 7 verify the locally bipartite and K4-free 8-degenerate branches. However, the Δ≤7 branch invokes the authorized source's Theorem 1.3, whose proof expressly depends on a catalogue of 1,144 external certificates and verifiers not contained in either authorized JSON; the paper says it supplies no human-readable proof of that catalogue. The mad<7 branch is likewise cited as Puleo's theorem without its proof in the authorized material. Under the requested independent-from-scratch standard, these two branches lack a rigorously checkable proof from the permitted evidence. No counterexample was found, so the claim is unresolved rather than refuted.
claims.search_method: Disjunct-by-disjunct dependency audit, including inspection of the authorized source's stated computational proof boundary.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either τ(G)≤2ν(G) for every finite simple graph or an explicit graph with a rigorous proof that τ(G)>2ν(G). The draft explicitly says the unrestricted conjecture is unresolved and supplies neither of those outcomes. Its nine-vertex graph is only non-WKE, not a counterexample to Tuza's inequality. Nevertheless, claims 0–9 rigorously establish material restricted results, notably the inequality when G△ is K4-free and 8-degenerate, and consequently when it is K4-free with mad(G△)<9; these are nonvacuous classes and may have unbounded maximum degree. Thus the draft makes valid but incomplete progress. Its claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is ACCURATE, not a full-resolution claim. Claim 10's additional source-dependent branches remain independently unresolved under the permitted evidence, but that does not erase the verified partial theorem.
